correctness.rationale: PASS. For every good \((x,y)\), direct expansion gives \((x+y)w-v^2=xy(b-c)^2\). In odd characteristic, for each \(v\) the affine map from \(w\) to \(R\) is bijective and the square map has one zero preimage and two preimages for each nonzero square, yielding exactly \(q\) fibers of size one and \(q(q-1)/2\) of size two. In characteristic two, Frobenius squaring is bijective, yielding a unique \((b,c)\) for every \((v,w)\). The good-set count is \((q-1)(q-2)\), and substitution into Eq. (16) gives the claimed formulas. The bundled checker reconstructs fibers over representative prime and extension fields; enumeration is supplementary to the analytic proof.

value.rationale: PASS. The source's result guarantees only constant success. The exact formula shows that the same two-copy quadratic measurement is asymptotically almost certain over characteristic-two fields but has a sharp \(1/2\) plateau over odd-characteristic fields. This is a structural algorithm-performance distinction caused by finite-field arithmetic, not a routine parameter substitution, and it identifies when the published lower-bound analysis hides a factor-of-two asymptotic gap or an approach to unit success.
